label: The Epistle to the Colossians addresses the church at Colossae

date.note: Traditional Pauline dating from an imprisonment (c. 55–62), which Harnack assumes. If Colossians is deutero-Pauline the letter shifts to c. 70–80, still attesting a community and still pre-Trajan.

secondary.cite: Harnack, Mission and Expansion, vol. 2, pp. 185–186

notes: Colossae in the Lycus valley (Pleiades 638811), near Laodicea and Hierapolis. Contemporary grade: the letter addresses a living church.
